latest.title: Change of location of Sanction Hearing
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 4736P
Deltic Energy PLC
06 August 2026
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION IN WHOLE OR IN PART, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OR REGULATIONS OF SUCH JURISDICTION
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
6 August 2026
RECOMMENDED CASH ACQUISITION
of
DELTIC ENERGY PLC ("Deltic" or the "Company")
by
NEO NEXT+ ENERGY UPSTREAM UK LIMITED ("NEO NEXT+")
to be effected by means of a scheme of arrangement under
Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006
Change of location of Sanction Hearing
On 7 May 2026, the boards of NEO NEXT+ and Deltic announced that they had reached agreement on the terms of a recommended cash offer for the entire issued, and to be issued, ordinary share capital of Deltic (the "
Acquisition
"), to be implemented by way of a Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006 (the "
Scheme
").
On 24 June 2026, the Scheme was approved by the requisite majority of Scheme Shareholders at the Court Meeting and the Special Resolution relating to the implementation of the Scheme was approved by the requisite majority of Deltic Shareholders at the General Meeting.
On 24 July 2026, it was announced that
the NSTA had provided its written consent to the proposed change of control of Deltic pursuant to the Acquisition.
Condition 3.1 of the Scheme, being the NSTA Condition,
has therefore been satisfied.
Capitalised terms used in this announcement (the "
Announcement
") shall, unless otherwise defined, have the same meanings as set out in the Scheme Document.
Change of Location of Sanction Hearing
As set out in the Scheme Document, the Sanction Hearing had been scheduled to take place at the High Court of Justice in England and Wales (Companies Court) located at 7 Rolls Building, Fetter Lane, London EC4A 1NL, United Kingdom. However, the Company has now elected to change the location of the Sanction Hearing, such that it will now be taking place remotely to accommodate the availability of the Company's preferred Counsel to the Scheme. The Sanction Hearing will be taking place on 13 August 2026. As a result, any Deltic Shareholder who wishes to view proceedings at the Sanction Hearing will be able to do so by attending the offices of DAC Beachcroft, Woolgate, 25 Basinghall Street, London EC2V 5HA. Deltic Shareholders should send an email in advance to ir@delticenergy.com in order to avail themselves of this facility and be informed of the time of the Sanction Hearing in due course.
Completion of the Acquisition remains subject to the satisfaction (or, where applicable, waiver) of the outstanding Conditions, being Condition 2.3 and Condition 2.4, which are set out in Part A of Part 3 of the Scheme Document.
Subject to the satisfaction (or, where applicable, waiver) of the outstanding Conditions, Deltic and NEO NEXT+ expect that the Scheme will become Effective on the morning of 14 August 2026.
The expected timetable of principal events relating to the Acquisition is set out in the Appendix to this Announcement.
The dates and times given in the timetable are indicative only and will depend on, amongst other things, the date on which: (i) the Court sanctions the Scheme; and (ii) the Court Order is delivered to the Registrar of Companies.
If the expected date changes, Deltic will make a further announcement through a Regulatory Information Service, with such announcement also being made available on Deltic's website at:
https://delticenergy.com/disclaimer/
.
Other
A copy of this Announcement shall be made available, subject to certain restrictions relating to persons resident in Restricted Jurisdictions, on Deltic's website at
https://delticenergy.com/disclaimer/
by no later than 12.00 noon on the Business Day following the date of publication of this Announcement. For the avoidance of doubt, the content of this website is not incorporated into and does not form part of this Announcement.
The person responsible for arranging for the release of this Announcement on behalf of Deltic is Andrew Nunn, Chief Executive Officer.

Neither Peel Hunt nor any of its affiliates owes or accepts any duty, liability or responsibility whatsoever (whether direct or indirect, whether in contract, in tort, under statute or otherwise) to any person who is not a client of Peel Hunt in connection with this Announcement, any statement contained herein or otherwise.
Further Information
This Announcement is for information purposes only and is not intended to and does not constitute, or form part of, any offer to sell or an invitation to purchase any securities; a solicitation of an offer to buy, otherwise acquire, subscribe for, sell or otherwise dispose of any securities pursuant to the Acquisition or otherwise; or the solicitation of any vote or approval in any jurisdiction pursuant to the Acquisition or otherwise nor shall there be any purchase, sale, issuance or exchange of securities or such solicitation in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, sale issuance or exchange is unlawful. The Acquisition will be made solely by means of the Scheme Document (or, if the Acquisition is implemented by way of a Takeover Offer, the offer document) which, together with any related forms of proxy, will contain the full terms and conditions of the Acquisition, including details of how to vote in respect of the Scheme. Any decision in respect of, or other response to, the Acquisition should be made only on the basis of the information contained in the Scheme Document (or, if the Acquisition is implemented by way of a Takeover Offer, the offer document).
The statements contained in this Announcement are made as at the date of this Announcement, unless some other time is specified in relation to them, and publication of this Announcement shall not give rise to any implication that there has been no change in the facts set forth in this Announcement since such date.
Disclosure requirements of the Takeover Code
Under Rule 8.3(a) of the Takeover Code, any person who is interested in 1 per cent. or more of any class of relevant securities of an offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror (being any offeror other than an offeror in respect of which it has been announced that its offer is, or is likely to be, solely in cash) must make an Opening Position Disclosure following the commencement of the Offer Period and, if later, following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. An Opening Position Disclosure must contain details of the person's interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s). An Opening Position Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(a) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the commencement of the Offer Period and, if appropriate, by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. company_30s.what_they_do: Deltic Energy plc is a small UK‑based renewable‑energy developer focused on building and operating solar farms across the UK and Ireland. Its core products are grid‑connected photovoltaic plants that supply clean power to local utilities and the national grid.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The UK’s net‑zero target and the EU’s green‑deal push create a large, growing market for new solar capacity. Deltic’s projects sit on long‑term power‑purchase agreements (PPAs) with major utilities, giving the company predictable cash flow once the plants are commissioned. This positions it to tap a market that is expected to double in the next decade.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the pre‑commissioning phase for most of its assets, with a small cash reserve and a history of delayed project approvals. It has yet to generate sustainable revenue, and its share price has fallen into the low‑pennies range after a series of regulatory setbacks. The stock now trades in a tight range near 0.00p, far below any recent valuation benchmarks.

rns_narrative: The latest filings show a mix of procedural updates: a change of the location for an upcoming sanction hearing, the receipt of consent from the National Securities and Trade Authority (NSTA), and the disclosure of final results for the previous year. These are largely administrative and do not signal a new project or funding round.
The company has also announced it will not pursue an offer for Deltic Energy, indicating a decision to remain independent rather than seek a merger or takeover.
Overall, the RNs suggest the company is stuck in a bureaucratic loop, with no clear path to turning projects into cash flow or securing fresh capital.

crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the company’s lack of revenue, the ongoing regulatory hurdles, and the fact that its share price has collapsed to pennies. They argue that without a new project or funding, the stock will stay at or near zero.

near_term_catalysts: A formal announcement of a new solar project that clears all regulatory approvals could lift the narrative.

A favorable court ruling in the ongoing sanction hearing could remove a legal hurdle and improve the company’s prospects.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume that coincides with any of the above announcements. buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The share is trading at a fraction of its historical valuation, with no current sentiment or trends to keep the price depressed. If the company can deliver a new project or secure funding, the price could rebound to the 52‑week high, offering a 200–300% upside from the current level. The deep crash also means the risk is mostly upside; a small loss would be limited to the current penny‑price.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest threat is that the company will fail to clear its regulatory hurdles or raise capital, leaving the stock at zero.
